questions.question: What is the entropy of a fair binary variable, using log base 2?
options: 1 bit
0 bits
2 bits
0.5 bits
questions.explanation: H(X) = -2*(0.5 log2 0.5) = 1. A fair coin has one bit of uncertainty.

questions.question: How are cross-entropy, entropy, and KL divergence related for true distribution p and model q?
options: CE(p,q) = H(q) - KL(p||q)
CE(p,q) = H(p) + KL(p||q)
KL(p||q) = H(p) + H(q) for all p and q
Cross-entropy is always smaller than entropy
questions.explanation: Cross-entropy decomposes into the irreducible entropy of p plus the mismatch penalty KL(p||q). The penalty is nonnegative and vanishes when the distributions match.

questions.question: Which property of KL divergence matters when comparing a model distribution with the target?
options: It is a true metric with the same value after swapping p and q
It can be negative whenever q assigns high probability
It is nonnegative and is zero only when the distributions agree, but it is not symmetric
It is symmetric whenever p and q have the same support
questions.explanation: Gibbs' inequality gives KL >= 0. In general KL(p||q) differs from KL(q||p), so the direction of the comparison is part of the definition.

questions.question: What is mutual information I(X;Y) when X and Y are independent?
options: H(X)+H(Y)
1 for every pair of variables
The larger of H(X) and H(Y)
questions.explanation: Independence means p(x,y)=p(x)p(y), so the log ratio in mutual information is zero everywhere with positive mass.

questions.question: A language model has entropy ln(4). What perplexity does that correspond to?
options: ln(4)
questions.explanation: Perplexity is exp(cross-entropy) when using natural logs. exp(ln 4)=4, the effective number of equally likely choices.

questions.question: A language model's average cross-entropy falls while its evaluation data stays fixed. What should happen to perplexity?
options: It rises because better likelihood means more uncertainty
It falls because perplexity is the exponential of cross-entropy
It stays exactly one for every model
It changes only if the vocabulary is reordered
questions.explanation: Perplexity = exp(cross-entropy) for natural-log loss, so a lower loss means a lower effective branching factor.
